intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency is caused by homozygous mutation in the gene encoding malonyl-CoA decarboxylase (MLYCD; 606761).

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency is caused by homozygous mutation in the gene encoding malonyl-CoA decarboxylase (MLYCD).
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified two different homozygous mutations in human MCD (hMCD) by using RT-PCR analysis of fibroblast RNA from two previously reported consanguineous Scottish patients with MCD deficiency.
checks.explanation: The abstract reports homozygous MCD mutations in patients with MCD deficiency. It says these mutations would be expected to cause the deficiency and that they segregated within the families.

paragraphs.text: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency is an extremely rare inborn error of metabolism (de Wit et al., 2006). Wightman et al. (2003) described it as an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by malonic aciduria, developmental delay, seizure disorder, hypoglycemia, and cardiomyopathy. It presents with metabolic acidosis, hypoglycemia, and/or cardiomyopathy (de Wit et al., 2006), and has also been associated with developmental delay (Sacksteder et al., 1999), hypotonia (Gao et al., 1999), and vomiting (Haan et al., 1986). Sacksteder et al. (1999) noted that cytoplasmic malonyl-CoA is a potent inhibitor of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation and suggested that malonyl-CoA decarboxylase regulates mitochondrial fatty acid uptake and oxidation, a hypothesis supported by the resemblance of the deficiency phenotypes to those of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation disorders.

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency is an extremely rare inborn error of metabolism.
checks.evidence_quote: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase (MCD) deficiency is an extremely rare inborn error of metabolism
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.evidence_quote: is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by malonic aciduria, developmental delay, seizure disorder, hypoglycemia, and cardiomyopathy.
checks.explanation: The abstract lists exactly these features.

checks.evidence_quote: malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency, a lethal disorder characterized by cardiomyopathy and developmental delay

checks.evidence_quote: deficiency of the enzyme has been associated with mild mental retardation, seizures, hypotonia, cardiomyopathy, vomiting, hypoglycemia, metabolic acidosis, and malonic aciduria
checks.explanation: The abstract lists hypotonia among the features linked to malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency.

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency has been associated with vomiting.
checks.evidence_quote: He is mildly mentally retarded and presented with vomiting, a seizure, hypoglycaemia and mild metabolic acidosis during a urinary tract infection.
checks.explanation: The patient with MCD deficiency presented with vomiting.

checks.claim: Cytoplasmic malonyl-CoA is a potent inhibitor of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation.
checks.evidence_quote: tissues in which cytoplasmic malonyl-CoA is a potent inhibitor of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Sacksteder et al. (1999) suggested that malonyl-CoA decarboxylase regulates mitochondrial fatty acid uptake and oxidation.
checks.evidence_quote: Cytoplasmic MCD is positioned to play a role in the regulation of cytoplasmic malonyl-CoA abundance and, thus, of mitochondrial fatty acid uptake and oxidation.
checks.explanation: The authors propose this hypothesis.

checks.claim: The hypothesis that malonyl-CoA decarboxylase regulates mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation is supported by the resemblance of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency phenotypes to those of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation disorders.
checks.evidence_quote: This hypothesis is supported by the fact that malonyl-CoA decarboxylase-deficient patients display a number of phenotypes that are reminiscent of mitochondrial fatty acid oxidation disorders.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: The disorder has also been called MLYCD deficiency (Wightman et al., 2003).

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency has also been called MLYCD deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase (MLYCD) deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder
checks.explanation: The paper uses the term 'MLYCD deficiency', including in its title.

paragraphs.text: Brown et al. (1984) described a patient with deficiency of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase, an inborn error of metabolism not recognized previously. The child had repeated episodes of vomiting, some requiring hospitalization.

checks.claim: Brown et al. (1984) described a patient with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency, an inborn error of metabolism not previously recognized.
checks.evidence_quote: A patient is described with a deficiency of the mitochondrial enzyme, malonyl CoA decarboxylase - an inborn error of metabolism not recognized previously.
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

checks.claim: The child with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency described by Brown et al. (1984) had repeated episodes of vomiting, some requiring hospitalization.
checks.evidence_quote: in a child with repeated episodes of vomiting, some requiring hospitalization.
checks.explanation: The abstract says this directly.

paragraphs.text: Malonic aciduria is the characterizing biochemical feature of the disorder (Wightman et al., 2003). In a patient reported by Haan et al. (1986), the urine contained increased amounts of malonic and methylmalonic acids, and malonyl-CoA decarboxylase activity in cultured fibroblast extracts was deficient (4% of the mean control value).

checks.claim: Malonic aciduria is the characterizing biochemical feature of malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: characterized by malonic aciduria, developmental delay, seizure disorder, hypoglycemia, and cardiomyopathy.
checks.explanation: The paper lists malonic aciduria as one of several characterizing features. It does not single it out as 'the' characterizing biochemical feature.

checks.claim: The urine of the malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency patient reported by Haan et al. (1986) contained increased amounts of malonic acid and methylmalonic acid.
checks.evidence_quote: The urine contained increased amounts of malonic, methylmalonic, succinic, adipic, glutaric and suberic acids.
checks.explanation: The paper reports increased urinary malonic and methylmalonic acids, along with other acids.

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase activity in cultured fibroblast extracts from the patient reported by Haan et al. (1986) was deficient, at 4% of the mean control value.
checks.evidence_quote: Mitochondrial malonyl CoA decarboxylase activity in cultured fibroblast extracts was 4% of the mean control value.
checks.explanation: The figure matches. The paper specifies mitochondrial activity.

paragraphs.text: Wightman et al. (2003) described malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency as an autosomal recessive disorder. FitzPatrick et al. (1999) identified homozygous MLYCD mutations in 2 consanguineous Scottish patients.

checks.claim: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase (MLYCD) deficiency is an autosomal recessive disorder
checks.explanation: Stated directly in the abstract.

checks.claim: FitzPatrick et al. (1999) identified homozygous MLYCD mutations in 2 consanguineous Scottish patients with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: We have identified two different homozygous mutations in human MCD (hMCD) by using RT-PCR analysis of fibroblast RNA from two previously reported consanguineous Scottish patients with MCD deficiency.
checks.explanation: The abstract states this directly.

paragraphs.text: FitzPatrick et al. (1999) identified 2 different homozygous mutations in the MLYCD gene by RT-PCR analysis of fibroblast RNA from 2 previously reported consanguineous Scottish patients with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency.

checks.evidence_quote: We have identified two different homozygous mutations in human MCD (hMCD) by using RT-PCR analysis of fibroblast RNA from two previously reported consanguineous Scottish patients with MCD deficiency.

checks.evidence_quote: two previously reported consanguineous Scottish patients with MCD deficiency
checks.explanation: The abstract says the patients had been reported before.

paragraphs.text: Sacksteder et al. (1999) found a severe mutation in the MLYCD gene (c.947-948delTT) in a patient with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency.

checks.claim: Sacksteder et al. (1999) found the MLYCD mutation c.947-948delTT in a patient with malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency.
checks.evidence_quote: a malonyl-CoA decarboxylase-deficient patient has a severe mutation in the MCD gene (c.947-948delTT)
checks.explanation: MCD is the paper's name for the gene, and MLYCD is its approved symbol.

checks.claim: The MLYCD c.947-948delTT mutation is a severe mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: a malonyl-CoA decarboxylase-deficient patient has a severe mutation in the MCD gene (c.947-948delTT)
checks.explanation: The paper describes the mutation as severe.

paragraphs.text: Haan et al. (1986) found that their patient excreted only relatively small quantities of malonic, methylmalonic, and succinic acid in the urine when fed an isocaloric low-fat, high-carbohydrate diet.

checks.claim: When fed an isocaloric low-fat, high-carbohydrate diet, the malonyl-CoA decarboxylase deficiency patient reported by Haan et al. (1986) excreted only relatively small quantities of malonic, methylmalonic, and succinic acid in the urine.
checks.evidence_quote: Only relatively small quantities of malonic, methylmalonic and succinic acid were excreted in the urine when the boy was fed an isocaloric low fat, high carbohydrate diet.
checks.explanation: The claim restates the abstract directly.
